title: Runya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Bava Metzia 93b relates that Aivu deposited flax with Runya; Shevu (a thief’s name) came and snatched it from him. He came before Rav Nachman, who held him liable.

There, at 109a: Runya was Ravina’s tree-planter; Runya caused a loss, and Ravina dismissed him. Runya came before Rava and said to him, “Let the Master see what he is doing to me.” He said to him, “He does well.” In Bava Batra 5a: Ravina surrounded Runya on his four sides — he came before Rava.

Hyman argues that we need not say that there were two Runyas or that he lived long, for the incident was at the end of Rav Nachman’s days, and Ravina was Rava’s student, and Rava was Rav Nachman’s distinguished student; or possibly it is Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak.

notes.text: שתלא is a tree-planter. Runya caused the loss, Ravina dismissed him, and Runya appealed to Rava. The one-Runya chronology and possible Nachman bar Yitzchak identity remain Hyman’s alternatives.

The consulted Bava Metzia 93b directly names Aivu, Runya, the thief Shabu and Rav Nachman. The later planter and enclosure cases and the one-Runya chronology are retained as Hyman’s account; the alternatives do not independently establish a single identity or Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak identification.
